title: More Words with Two Meanings
objectives: I can tell that a word can have two meanings, in school and in play.
I can use the words around a word to choose its meaning.
I can use the same word in two different ways in my own sentences.
I can draw a picture for each meaning of a word.
rationale: Unit 3 introduced words with two meanings in nature and play. This unit adds eight everyday words from school and the neighborhood, which asks children to switch between meanings in sentences they hear and read all day. As in Unit 3, one meaning is the main sense and the second is taught on purpose. Two of the words, mean and kind, are also character words, so children connect the unit to the traits they used in Unit 11. The review words bark, spring, bank, and fly bring back the first set so children can tell that this is a pattern across the language.

words.def: To look at something for a time.

words.def: To bend down quickly to avoid something.

senses.example: A duck paddled across the pond.

senses.def: To stand for or show an idea.

words.ex2: It is mean to leave a friend out of the game.
words.nonExample: Sharing your snack is not mean.

cloze2.s: The ___ king in the story laughed at everyone who made a mistake.

senses.def: A type or sort of thing.

words.def: Treating everyone in the same way.

senses.example: We rode the Ferris wheel at the fair.

words.ex: It is fair to give each child one turn.
words.ex2: The referee was fair to both teams.
words.nonExample: Letting one person have all the turns is not fair.

cloze2.s: The judge was ___ and gave every team the same chance to win.

misuse.s: It was fair that one child got all the cookies and the others got none.

passage.title: A Day at the Fair
paras: Our class took a train to the fair. A kind man gave every child a ticket, and that was fair.
Kai had to duck under a rope to watch the games. He picked up a stick and drew a point on the dirt to show where to stand. A mean boy pushed in line, but the teacher made him wait.

qs.q: What does "fair" mean in the first sentence?
choices: a place with games and rides
qs.why: Our class took a train to the fair, so it is a place with games and rides.

qs.q: What did Kai do to see the games?
qs.why: The story says Kai had to duck under a rope to watch the games.

qs.q: Why was it fair that every child got a ticket?
qs.why: Fair means treating everyone the same, and every child got a ticket.

teacher.overview: Children learn eight everyday words that each have two meanings, in school and play settings. The main sense is taught first and the second sense on purpose. Use quick picture pairs. Kind and mean connect to the character traits from Unit 11. Revisit bark, spring, bank, and fly to show how common two-meaning words are.

notes.va.watch.v: Watch is a verb (to look) and a noun (a clock on the wrist). Show a real watch and a pair of eyes. Children may know it as a verb only. Spanish: mirar or observar for the verb, reloj for the noun.
notes.va.point.n: Point is the sharp tip first and a game score second. Teach point to mean a tip with a pencil, a pin, and a nail. The verb to point with a finger is a third sense and can come up; do not teach it here.
notes.va.train.n: Train is a vehicle first and a verb meaning to practice second. Use a picture of a train and a picture of an athlete practicing. Cognate tren for the vehicle.
notes.va.stick.n: Stick is a thin branch first and a verb meaning to hold fast second. Show a stick and a glue stick. Past form of the verb is stuck; children may find it irregular.
notes.va.duck.v: Duck is an action first and a bird second. Show both with a picture and with movement. Children often know the bird first; act out the verb for them.
notes.va.mean.adj: Mean here is unkind. The verb mean (to show or stand for) is the second sense. Keep the focus on actions, not people. Contrast with kind.
notes.va.kind.adj: Kind is caring first and a type or sort second. Show I like this kind of fruit. Kind is a trait word from Unit 11; connect.
notes.va.fair.adj: Fair is treating everyone the same first and a place with games second. Use turn-taking examples. Fair is also a weather and skin word; do not teach those here.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The sentence says Kai had to duck under the rope. The rope is low and Kai has to bend down. A duck bird cannot bend under a rope, so this duck is the action. The clue words rope and under help me.'
discuss: Which clue words in a sentence help you choose a meaning?
Which two-meaning word from this unit is the hardest to picture twice?
misconceptions: Children may think each word has only one meaning. Show two pictures together.
Some children think mean is a name for a person. Keep it on actions: that was a mean thing to do.
Children may mix up kind (caring) with kind (type) because both sound the same; use clue words like nurse and fruit.
extend: Make a class chart with a picture and a sentence for each meaning.
Find a two-meaning word in a read-aloud and decide which meaning the author used.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit bark, spring, bank, and fly from Unit 3: ask children to tell a sentence for each meaning and compare with the words in this unit.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (mirar, punta, tren, palo, agacharse, malo, amable, justo) not reviewed by a native speaker; they give the main sense only.
point (tip) and fair (equal) also have other common senses (to point, a fair day); only the two taught senses are claimed.
